audited_findings.result: An untrained hosted 8B reader did not reliably execute the CC7/CC8 state-reading task from natural, JSON, readable ClayCode or aggressive ClayCode projections. One V2 run reached 6/10 on named and positional JSON, while stricter V3/V4 replications remained brittle and frequently copied ids/activations or ignored the requested mapping. Readable ClayCode reduced prompt-token cost versus named JSON in the V2 arm (328 vs 573 prompt tokens, about 42.8% less) but did not preserve reliable task correctness; aggressive compact ClayCode also failed zero-shot.
audited_findings.interpretation: Compression alone is not sufficient small-model usability. Preserve canonical semantic IR and develop reader-specific projections, deterministic interpreters/parsers, few-shot adapters or target-model internalization. This does not refute ClayCode; it refutes assuming zero-shot compact syntax is already a safe small-model interface.
audited_findings.falsifier_or_next_test: Repeat the same fixed gold corpus on the actual Qwen3-4B target with tokenizer-matched JSON, readable ClayCode and trained/few-shot reader projections; compare semantic accuracy, repair rate and tokens per correct answer.

audited_findings.result: On the fixed 12-case freshness/authority corpus, the explicit semantic arm scored 9/12 (75%) with 1 unsafe ACCEPT; compact Gamma scored 3/12 (25%) with 2 unsafe ACCEPTs; compact OTCC scored 5/12 (41.7%) and produced 7 unsafe ACCEPTs, including an all-ACCEPT failure pattern.
audited_findings.interpretation: Safety-critical freshness/capability/closure decisions must remain deterministic host/runtime semantics. Compact model-readable Gamma/OTCC forms are not safe zero-shot authority surfaces on this proxy. Model outputs remain proposals, never authority.
audited_findings.falsifier_or_next_test: A target 4B reader with a deterministic projection or trained decoder must reach zero unsafe ACCEPTs over adversarial closure/capability cases before any model-mediated safety fast path is considered.

audited_findings.result: Raw-output audit of the GWT reconstruction proxy shows 8/8 semantic recovery from the full semantic projection and 8/8 from the compact projection; a deliberately scrambled projection produced 0/8 truth accuracy while faithfully following the supplied corruption; transport-receipt-only context produced no true semantic recovery and induced placeholder/confabulated output rather than justified UNKNOWN.
audited_findings.interpretation: Transport/read success is distinct from semantic reconstruction and uptake. A downstream model can faithfully consume a corrupt projection, so projection identity/integrity/freshness must be verified separately. GWT instrumentation should separate transport receipt -> projection/reconstruction -> uptake -> effect/outcome.
audited_findings.falsifier_or_next_test: Hold FRANK transport constant while lesioning/shuffling semantic projection into the actual Core/Qwen reader and measure inclusion, uptake and effects.

audited_findings.result: Audited eight-item matched-content proxy: neutral accuracy 7/8 (87.5%), reversed option ordering 5/8 (62.5%), truthful WINNER metadata 7/8 (87.5%), false WINNER metadata 6/8 (75%). Raw-answer comparison shows three flips under reversed order, two under truthful winner labeling and one under false winner labeling relative to neutral.
audited_findings.interpretation: Even temperature-zero small-model decisions are materially context/order/metadata sensitive. GWT/FRANK experiments must counterbalance order and independently shuffle/truth-test winner metadata; a workspace winner label cannot be treated as ground truth for downstream uptake/effect attribution.
audited_findings.falsifier_or_next_test: Run larger counterbalanced target-model corpus with randomized option/order/winner metadata and paired seeds; estimate effect sizes and interaction with task difficulty.

audited_findings.result: Across V3/V4 reader replications, role-labelled relation-instance edges were more recoverable than function-like n-ary syntax in this hosted 8B reader. V4 raw reified output recovered six of eight sender/recipient relations while function-style n-ary output recovered two of eight before returning UNKNOWN for the rest. The naive pairwise arm is not a valid positive control because input ordering leaked sender/recipient order and must not be interpreted as preserving n-ary semantics.
audited_findings.interpretation: Keep n-ary semantics in the canonical graph/IR where needed, but prefer explicit relation-instance + role-labelled edge projections for small-model readers. This aligns with H2's independent synthetic/formal ambiguity result without counting it as independent replication of the same model test.
audited_findings.falsifier_or_next_test: Use randomized role ordering and symmetric pairwise baselines with no positional role leakage, then compare n-ary, reified role-labelled and lossy pairwise representations on the target 4B.

audited_findings.result: On GitHub-runner self-use, current ClayGraph activation/lexical retrieval took roughly 84-87 ms median per query versus about 0.8-0.9 ms for SQLite FTS and generally supplied larger contexts. The current graph/lexical modes surfaced some cross-branch relational facts that SQLite FTS missed on the small audited QA set, but activation did not consistently beat graph-lexical selection and sometimes added noise. Automatic answer-hit scoring was too brittle, so promotion is based on the audited engineering pattern rather than that invalid metric.
audited_findings.interpretation: Do not place the current Python activation overlay in FRANK's hot path. Keep ClayGraph as a derived semantic/associative research substrate, optimize seed/index/edge weighting and assembly compression, and test whether it can select compact Topic/Micro-Packets better than deterministic envelopes. The current candidate is HOLD, not PROMOTE.
audited_findings.falsifier_or_next_test: A next ClayGraph generation must beat the deterministic packet-envelope/SQLite baselines on audited multi-hop recall or decision quality without unacceptable latency/context regression, then replicate on live/twin FRANK store traces.

clay.summary: Add reader-specific projection and context-selection cost to Synthetic Clay optimization objectives; do not equate semantic compactness with usable small-model cognition.

frank.summary: Keep deterministic authority/closure semantics outside model self-authorization; require projection integrity and counterbalanced winner/order controls; keep current ClayGraph activation out of hot path pending better evidence.

gwt.summary: Strengthens the need to separate transport, reconstruction, uptake and effect; adds direct small-model evidence for order/winner confounds.

emergenz.summary: No direct emergence mechanism was tested. Methodologically, future small-model emergence experiments should counterbalance representation/order effects.

claycode.summary: Zero-shot compact/readable projections are not yet reliable; safety-critical compact semantics are unsafe as model authority. Prioritize deterministic semantic IR, reader projection and target-reader training/internalization tests.

hyperposition.summary: Supports role-aware relation-instance projection for small-model readers while preserving n-ary semantics in canonical form; pairwise reader test requires non-leaky redesign.

claygraph.summary: Current activation candidate remains HOLD: relational coverage is promising but Python retrieval latency/context/noise currently lose badly to SQLite on hot-path cost.
